title: Checkout Citadel
tagline: The long journey: register, shop, check out, pay, and clean up after yourself.
teaches: Full end-to-end flows built from helpers, self-contained data, and teardown that always runs
objectives: Build a ten-step journey that still reads like a paragraph, because the steps are helpers
Create the data the test needs instead of depending on data somebody else left behind
Delete the account you created, even when the assertion in the middle failed
Assert at the points that matter, rather than after every single click
Judge when one long E2E test is right and when it should have been three short ones
plannedChallenges: Register, then shop: the journey in helpers
Self-contained data: your own account, every run
Assert at the checkpoints that matter
Fix the broken test: it checks out as the wrong user
Teardown that survives a mid-test failure
One long test or three short ones?
Boss: rebuild Test Case 16 - login, check out, verify the invoice, delete the account
